agents.verdict: Use concrete scenes as evidence, not repeated props.
agents.recommendation: Root each slide in the story's actual behavior, pose, or setting.

agents.verdict: Keep the romance scene on the unspoken emotional request.
agents.recommendation: Make every scene prove the emotional obstacle, not only the pretty surface.

agents.verdict: Approve only if the plan avoids one-setting repetition and keeps Zuv active.
agents.recommendation: Block generic couple stock poses, cluttered backgrounds, and prop-first storyboards.

options.name: Wordless Habit Relay + Broken-Key Continuity
options.case_for: Pairs an instantly readable mutual-habit hook with one staged incident whose object state and body distance carry the emotional turn.
options.risk: The continuous landing sequence needs a strict shot ladder and one wardrobe lock.

options.name: Domestic Evidence Montage
options.case_for: Multiple ordinary settings are immediately relatable.
options.risk: Generic list energy; no consequence earns the care turn.

options.name: Threshold Distance Ladder
options.case_for: Eye-lines, hands, and changing distance make anger and care coexist visibly.
options.risk: Too repetitive as a standalone system; retained as a supporting mechanic.

selector_verdict: Wordless Habit Relay + Broken-Key Continuity wins because automatic exchanges prove the hook, the snapped-key incident earns the turn, and the repaired-key relay closes the payoff without wedding clichés.
hard_fails_checked: home and doorway scenes are deliberate story architecture, not a generic default
story evidence must prove every locked line with text hidden
the snapped key appears only in the continuous middle and returns once as payoff consequence

final_visual_plan.copy:
We’re not married yet.
But try telling that to our habits.
final_visual_plan.visual: Wide three-quarter apartment doorway scene: Aachu slips Zuv's wallet and keys into his waiting jacket pocket while Zuv simultaneously lowers her filled water bottle into her open tote. Neither looks at the other; their crossed forearms and automatic timing prove muscle memory. Couple in lower half, clean ivory negative space above-left, brandmark clear top-right.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Every plan starts with:
“Ek minute, usse poochna padega.”
final_visual_plan.visual: Over-shoulder threshold view from outside: Aachu is halfway through the exit, one palm raised to the unseen outside world in a natural one-second gesture, while turning back toward Zuv. Zuv stands several feet inside holding two helmets and gives a familiar nod. The check-in reads as alignment, never permission.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Every small decision becomes
a two-person meeting.
final_visual_plan.visual: Wide profile hallway scene: Zuv holds a small blank framed print against the wall while Aachu stands several feet back, squinting with mock seriousness and pinching two fingers to signal two centimetres left. Their eye-lines converge on the frame; subtle painter's-tape alternatives show mutual over-investment without clutter.

Tight over-Zuv-shoulder landing shot at lock level: he remains upright, frozen at the apartment lock, holding half of a snapped key while the other half is unmistakably stuck. Aachu is not yet visible. The solitary reaction establishes one person's problem before it spreads.

High three-quarter landing view: the broken key remains in the lock. Both stay upright. Aachu searches her tote for a spare or maintenance number while Zuv lights the lock with his phone torch and examines it without forcing it. Their shoulders nearly touch and both eye-lines fix on the same obstacle; neither rescues the other.

Low-medium two-shot along the same landing: Aachu holds out a blank maintenance card while Zuv holds the snapped key and argues for another solution. They stand two to three feet apart with direct eye-line, equal irritation, open palms, and no finger-pointing. The failed lock sits between their competing solutions.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Then five minutes later:
“Ghar pahunch ke text karna.”
final_visual_plan.visual: Wide view from inside the now-open doorway toward the stairwell: Zuv is already two steps down, body facing away with helmet in hand. Aachu remains in the doorway, posture still stiff, but instinctively calls after him. He stops mid-step and turns back immediately; their eye-lines reconnect across the distance.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Kyunki gussa apni jagah.
“Tum theek ho?” apni jagah.
final_visual_plan.visual: Intimate waist-up profile at the threshold: both still look mildly annoyed and avoid a romantic gaze. Aachu notices a tiny nick on Zuv's thumb from the broken key and offers a tissue while Zuv keeps his other arm completely outside the frame; no hand touches or braces the door. Zuv stands fully in front of the door and doorframe; a continuous visible contour separates his hair, shoulder, back, shirt, and torso from both solid surfaces. No door or frame line touches, crosses, replaces, or absorbs any part of his body. Their simultaneous gestures show anger and concern occupying the same frame; their hands nearly meet without an embrace.

Very wide architectural landing shot: Aachu stands inside her doorway and Zuv pauses several steps away near the stairs, still connected by eye-line and each holding one of the other's everyday belongings. The physical space honestly shows two separate lives; the exchanged objects show the unofficial unit already operating.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Shaadi abhi baaki hai.
Par “hum” toh kab ke ban chuke hain.
final_visual_plan.visual: Circular visual echo of slide 1 on another morning and in different clothes: at the same doorway, Aachu passes Zuv his wallet while Zuv passes her water bottle in the same automatic crossed-hand relay. This time a repaired key hangs quietly beside the door and both share the smallest knowing smile. The visual closes the story through repeated behavior, not a wedding symbol or generic embrace.
